study_design: Randomized controlled clinical trial with follow-up for incident prostate cancer
cohort_total_n_excerpt: We randomly assigned 672 men to receive either 3 g of calcium carbonate (1,200 mg of calcium), or placebo, daily for 4 years in a colorectal adenoma chemoprevention trial.
reason: The trial analyzed incident overall prostate cancer. Although the abstract states that most cases were not advanced, it does not report an exposure association for advanced or another aggressive prostate cancer endpoint.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Baseline dietary calcium intake, plasma 1,25-(OH)2 vitamin D and 25-(OH) vitamin D levels were not materially associated with risk.
estimate_classifications.reason: This row concerns vitamin D biomarkers and the abstract reports their associations with overall prostate cancer risk, without an aggressive endpoint.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: After a mean follow-up of 10.3 years, there were 33 prostate cancer cases in the calcium-treated group and 37 in the placebo-treated group [unadjusted rate ratio, 0.83; 95% confidence interval (95% CI), 0.52-1.32].
estimate_classifications.reason: The estimate is for overall incident prostate cancer comparing calcium supplementation with placebo.
